newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-PIENAAR ON LOSING SIDE IN DEBUT MATCH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-PIENAAR ON LOSING SIDE IN DEBUT MATCH.

text.p: Francois Pienaar finished on the losing side on his English rugby union debut, but only after league champions Bath survived a stunning late fightback by the former South Africa captain's new side Saracens.

Saracens had looked down and out midway through the second half as Bath stormed into a 35-14 lead but Pienaar and his fellow forwards dug deep, hauling the London club to within a two points of their opponents.

Captain Tony Diprose, wing Richard Wallace and flanker Gary Clark all crossed the Bath line during a tense final quarter when Saracens scored 19 points in the last 20 minutes and looked capable of achieving the seemingly impossible.
There had seemed no way back for Saracens, especially as Australian fly-half Michael Lynagh's kicking form deserted him after he had landed three early penalty shots.

But then Pienaar began to show up more in open play, and when he linked with French centre Phillipe Sella in midfield, Canadian wing Courtney Smith marked his league debut by handing off opposite number Jon Sleightholme to score wide out.
In the end, Bath were hanging on to stave off a fourth league defeat which could have proved fatal in their quest to retain the title.
